meaning: Harmful software that locks your files or your device. The crook then demands payment to unlock them.
clues: It holds something of yours hostage.
The thing held hostage is your files, or your whole device.
A message on the screen says you must pay to get your stuff back.
Even if you pay, there is no promise you will get your files back.
It has ten letters and starts with R. The first part is a word for money paid to free a hostage.
assumes: Spyware secretly watches what you do
Antivirus software scans for harmful programs

decoys.meaning: Hidden software that secretly watches what you do on a device and sends it to someone else.
Software that scans a device for harmful programs and removes them.
A spare copy of your files, kept in a second place in case the first copy is lost.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: We always kept a spare copy of important files on a second disk. That old habit still works.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: It really does. A backup means a crook holding your files hostage has much less power over you.

sources.name: FTC, Malware: How To Protect Against, Detect, and Remove It
